pathway.title: Block, Inc. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, Block's liquidity is its main credit support: cash and cash equivalents of USD 7,859.3 million and an undrawn USD 900.0 million revolver exceed total debt of USD 7,318.5 million, and no note matures before the USD 575.0 million convertible in November 2027, so near-term refinancing exposure is mostly in the secured warehouse lines, whose final maturities are USD 515.0 million in 2027 (USD 447.4 million of it classified current), rather than the bond stack. Second, leverage is highly sensitive to the earnings definition: filed-basis total debt to EBITDA rose from 4.19x at FY2025 to 4.67x at LTM Q3 2026 while interest cover fell from 8.44x to 3.99x, whereas management's basis shows 1.69x and 11.03x; the add-backs include contingencies, restructuring and other charges and share-based compensation, so the covenant outcome cannot be inferred. Third, legal claims sit outside the debt figures: USD 764 million is accrued for the Department of Justice matter, accrued legal contingencies rose from USD 173.0 million to USD 980.6 million, and the filing says losses above the accrual are reasonably possible; a USD 150 million insurer payment in the derivative settlement is a possible partial offset but is not final. Fourth, reported operating cash flow less capital expenditure of USD 3,453.4 million over the LTM period is flattered by this unpaid accrual and excludes lending outflows. Fifth, lending growth increases funding reliance on secured warehouse borrowings of USD 1,543.5 million and brokered certificates of deposit of USD 381.4 million, which rank ahead of unsecured note holders on those assets and depend on the bank subsidiary remaining well capitalized.

runs.text: Strengths. (1) Liquidity and maturity profile, Documentary Fact: stated liquidity of USD 10,064.0 million, the undrawn revolver maturing in January 2031, note maturities spread from 2027 to 2033 and the 2026 maturities of USD 1,575.0 million repaid in cash, which supports debt service without market access (an Analyst Interpretation). (2) Gross profit mix, Documentary Fact: payments and lending drive gross profit while bitcoin revenue, 27% of Q3 2026 revenue, contributes 2% of gross profit, so bitcoin price swings change revenue more than earnings. (3) Fixed-rate unsecured note stack, Analyst Interpretation: coupons from 0.25% to 6.50% give a run-rate annual coupon of USD 293.9 million on USD 5,775.0 million of principal, about 18.8% of the add-back-free LTM EBITDA of USD 1,567.0 million (a calculated share), so the fixed charge looks manageable if earnings hold.

Weaknesses. (1) Add-back dependence, Documentary Fact for the figures and Analyst Interpretation for the reading: Adjusted EBITDA of USD 4,336.4 million is more than double filed EBITDA of USD 1,567.0 million, and contingencies charges recur across 2026 quarters, so the add-backs are not one-off in the period. (2) Unpaid legal claims, Documentary Fact: the accrual and the possibility of excess losses are claims outside debt that will draw on cash, and the final agreement and court approval are pending. (3) Credit losses in a growing lending book, Documentary Fact: transaction, loan and consumer receivable losses were USD 601.7 million in Q3 2026 against USD 363.5 million a year earlier, which reduces operating income directly. (4) Customer cash, Analyst Interpretation: customers payable exceed customer funds by USD 2,343.2 million before USD 1,454.2 million of settlements receivable, a residual of USD 889.0 million that corporate cash may fund, so net debt of negative USD 540.8 million may overstate surplus cash. (5) Control and capital allocation, Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation: Class B holders control a majority of votes, and share repurchases of USD 700.9 million in 2026 compete with deleveraging for the same cash.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: There is no transaction document, sponsor, use-of-proceeds statement or acquisition financing for 2026 in the sources, so no transaction row is built beyond the financing history below; that absence is Insufficient Information, not an adverse conclusion.

New debt issues. In the nine months of 2026 the company issued no senior notes: the cash flow statement shows no proceeds from issuance of senior notes for 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:8). The last note issue was on August 18, 2025, when 2.2 billion of senior unsecured notes were issued, comprising 1.2 billion of 2030 Senior Notes at 5.625% and 1.0 billion of 2033 Senior Notes at 6.000% (10-K page:188). The 2032 Senior Notes, 2.0 billion at 6.50%, were issued on May 9, 2024 (10-K page:190). In 2025 the company recorded 2.3 billion of share repurchases alongside the 2.2 billion of cash received from that issuance (10-K page:111); the filing does not say the proceeds funded the repurchases, so the link is an Analyst Interpretation of timing only.

Repayments and facility changes. The 2026 Convertible Notes (575.0) were paid in cash at maturity on May 1, 2026 and the 2026 Senior Notes (1,000.0) on June 1, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:27), leaving note principal of 5,775.0 across the 2027 Convertible Notes and the 2030, 2031, 2032 and 2033 Senior Notes. On January 14, 2026 the revolving credit agreement was amended and restated, raising commitments from 775 to 900, extending maturity to January 14, 2031 with a springing earlier date if liquidity would fall below 250 after repaying existing notes at maturity, and replacing the prior financial covenant with a maximum total net leverage ratio tested quarterly; the revolver is undrawn (10-Q Q3 page:28). Warehouse borrowings stood at 1,543.5, with a total of 2.4 billion of capacity and 809.3 available, and final maturities through July 2029 (10-Q Q3 page:29). Brokered certificates of deposit of 381.4 par began in Q3 2026 at a weighted average rate of 4.09% (10-Q Q3 page:56).

Subsequent events and pending items (after the September 30, 2026 balance sheet date, before the November 3, 2026 filing and the cutoff). In October 2026 the company and the Department of Justice reached an agreement in principle to resolve the Bank Secrecy Act inquiry by a three-year deferred prosecution agreement, with a gross monetary component of approximately 964 million and a net payment of approximately 764 million after credit for prior regulatory resolutions; 764 million was accrued at September 30, 2026, and the resolution remains subject to a final agreement and court approval (10-Q Q3 page:34). The filing says losses in excess of the accrual are reasonably possible (10-Q Q3 page:35). Also in October 2026 the parties to the shareholder derivative actions agreed in principle to a global resolution including a 150 million payment from the defendants' insurers to the company, subject to court approval (10-Q Q3 page:36). The securities class action remains pending after the motion to dismiss was denied on January 6, 2026, with an accrual that the filing calls not material and a possible loss in excess that could be material (10-Q Q3 page:35). These items are subsequent events or pending matters and are not folded into period facts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Block, Inc. reports a platform business with two reportable segments and a revenue base that grew in 2026 on payments volume and consumer lending. Its debt at September 30, 2026 consists of five note series (four senior unsecured series and one convertible series) with 5,775.0 of principal, secured warehouse borrowings of 1,543.5 held in special purpose entities whose assets are not available to the issuer's creditors, and an undrawn 900.0 revolver. Cash and cash equivalents of 7,859.3 exceed total debt of 7,318.5, so net debt is negative on that measure. On the filed basis (operating income plus depreciation and amortization, no add-backs) LTM EBITDA is 1,567.0, giving total debt to EBITDA of 4.67x, up from 4.19x at FY2025, and EBITDA to cash interest of 3.99x, down from 8.44x. On management's Adjusted EBITDA of 4,336.4 the same ratios are 1.69x and 11.03x. The gap between the two bases is mostly share-based compensation (about 1.2 billion a year) and "contingencies, restructuring and other charges", which were 1,542.9 for nine months 2026 (742.8 + 365.1 + 435.0). Separately, accrued legal contingencies on the balance sheet rose to 980.6 at the latest quarter from 173.0 at FY2025, and include 764 for a Department of Justice resolution agreed in principle in October 2026 and accrued at September 30, 2026. That payment is a cash claim outside the debt figure. The reported cash flow is flattered by the unpaid accrual. The view is therefore moderate gross leverage with ample stated liquidity, a bond maturity profile with nothing due until November 2027, and meaningful non-debt claims and definition risk that the covenant (a maximum total net leverage ratio, level not printed) cannot be tested against from the pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Block, Inc. is an operating company with two reportable segments, Square for sellers and Cash App for consumers, and a third revenue lens of commerce enablement, financial solutions and bitcoin ecosystem. It has no sponsor, no leveraged transaction and no acquisition financing in the sources. The transaction history that matters to creditors is a series of unsecured note issues (the 2032 notes in 2024, the 2030 and 2033 notes on August 18, 2025), the repayment in cash of two 2026 maturities, the January 14, 2026 amendment that enlarged the revolver and replaced its financial covenant with a maximum total net leverage ratio, a larger share repurchase authorization, and, after the quarter end but before the filing, agreements in principle on a Department of Justice deferred prosecution matter and a derivative-suit settlement. Control rests with Class B holders with ten votes per share, and the founder is described as controlling shareholder in the bank-regulatory commitments for Square Financial Services. Documented issuer behaviour is Neutral or Mixed: debt was repaid from cash and the revolver enlarged, but repurchases continue and 2025 issuance occurred in a year of large repurchases. No priming, uptiering, drop-down, non-pro-rata exchange or collateral release appears in the pages read. The creditor mechanisms to watch are lending growth funded by secured warehouse lines (which sit ahead of note holders on those receivables), the unpaid legal settlements, and the absence of the executed documents that would show restricted payments capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Block, Inc. has a moderate credit profile: strong stated liquidity is set against leverage that looks high on filed earnings and low on management's adjusted earnings. The strongest support is liquidity: USD 7,859.3 million of cash and cash equivalents and an undrawn USD 900.0 million revolver, against USD 5,775.0 million of note principal and no note due before the 2027 convertible. The weakest point is earnings quality: total debt to EBITDA is 4.67x on the filed basis but 1.69x on management's Adjusted EBITDA, because share-based compensation and large legal charges are added back, while USD 764 million for the Department of Justice matter is accrued but unpaid. The outcome turns on the final size and timing of the legal payments, the unpublished covenant level and whether credit losses in the growing lending book stay contained.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, Block's liquidity is its main credit support: cash and cash equivalents of USD 7,859.3 million and an undrawn USD 900.0 million revolver exceed total debt of USD 7,318.5 million, and no note matures before the USD 575.0 million convertible in November 2027, so near-term refinancing exposure is mostly in the secured warehouse lines, whose final maturities are USD 515.0 million in 2027 (USD 447.4 million of it classified current), rather than the bond stack. Second, leverage is highly sensitive to the earnings definition: filed-basis total debt to EBITDA rose from 4.19x at FY2025 to 4.67x at LTM Q3 2026 while interest cover fell from 8.44x to 3.99x, whereas management's basis shows 1.69x and 11.03x; the add-backs include contingencies, restructuring and other charges and share-based compensation, so the covenant outcome cannot be inferred. Third, legal claims sit outside the debt figures: USD 764 million is accrued for the Department of Justice matter, accrued legal contingencies rose from USD 173.0 million to USD 980.6 million, and the filing says losses above the accrual are reasonably possible; a USD 150 million insurer payment in the derivative settlement is a possible partial offset but is not final. Fourth, reported operating cash flow less capital expenditure of USD 3,453.4 million over the LTM period is flattered by this unpaid accrual and excludes lending outflows. Fifth, lending growth increases funding reliance on secured warehouse borrowings of USD 1,543.5 million and brokered certificates of deposit of USD 381.4 million, which rank ahead of unsecured note holders on those assets and depend on the bank subsidiary remaining well capitalized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. (1) Liquidity and maturity profile, Documentary Fact: stated liquidity of USD 10,064.0 million, the undrawn revolver maturing in January 2031, note maturities spread from 2027 to 2033 and the 2026 maturities of USD 1,575.0 million repaid in cash, which supports debt service without market access (an Analyst Interpretation). (2) Gross profit mix, Documentary Fact: payments and lending drive gross profit while bitcoin revenue, 27% of Q3 2026 revenue, contributes 2% of gross profit, so bitcoin price swings change revenue more than earnings. (3) Fixed-rate unsecured note stack, Analyst Interpretation: coupons from 0.25% to 6.50% give a run-rate annual coupon of USD 293.9 million on USD 5,775.0 million of principal, about 18.8% of the add-back-free LTM EBITDA of USD 1,567.0 million (a calculated share), so the fixed charge looks manageable if earnings hold.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. (1) Add-back dependence, Documentary Fact for the figures and Analyst Interpretation for the reading: Adjusted EBITDA of USD 4,336.4 million is more than double filed EBITDA of USD 1,567.0 million, and contingencies charges recur across 2026 quarters, so the add-backs are not one-off in the period. (2) Unpaid legal claims, Documentary Fact: the accrual and the possibility of excess losses are claims outside debt that will draw on cash, and the final agreement and court approval are pending. (3) Credit losses in a growing lending book, Documentary Fact: transaction, loan and consumer receivable losses were USD 601.7 million in Q3 2026 against USD 363.5 million a year earlier, which reduces operating income directly. (4) Customer cash, Analyst Interpretation: customers payable exceed customer funds by USD 2,343.2 million before USD 1,454.2 million of settlements receivable, a residual of USD 889.0 million that corporate cash may fund, so net debt of negative USD 540.8 million may overstate surplus cash. (5) Control and capital allocation, Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation: Class B holders control a majority of votes, and share repurchases of USD 700.9 million in 2026 compete with deleveraging for the same cash.
